title: Observability at scale
task_statement: Rebuild any integration run from traces, usage data, and telemetry, without text logs alone. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Request tracing with OpenTelemetry
components.first_principle: A trace records each step of one run with a shared trace ID, so you can rebuild the run from the spans.

nodes.label: Your app starts the run span

steps: Set up SDK tracing with a tracer provider in your application.
Add an API tracing destination in the Claude Console.
Keep the metadata only content mode for routine exports.
Choose the full content mode only where your retention rules allow prompt storage.
Sum token usage from one source only, so each token counts once.
Check the truncated attribute before you read a long span.
pros: Each model run and tool use appears in one trace.
Any platform that accepts OTLP can receive the spans.
Token attributes on each span support cost per request.
cons: Full content stores prompts and responses in your observability platform.
Span delivery is best effort, so a span can be lost.
Content over the size limit is shortened and marked as truncated.
use_when: An incident needs the path of one request through several calls.
Cost per request or per feature must be attributed.
Your own application traces must link to Claude calls.
do_not_use_when: Your organization has a HIPAA, FERPA, or K-12 restriction and needs prompt text in API tracing, because those destinations export metadata only.
A single call with no tools needs only the prompt log.
The data path must guarantee every span, since delivery is best effort.

constraints.choice: Use metadata only for routine exports.
constraints.combination: Use full content for a narrow debug set with its own retention rule.

constraints.choice: Use full content with zero data retention, which holds exported content in memory only for Messages API requests.
constraints.combination: Claude Managed Agents is not eligible for zero data retention.

constraints.choice: Keep the default content limit of 0.75 MB per span.
constraints.combination: Raise the limit only when your platform accepts larger payloads.

constraints.choice: Sum the API spans for token totals on API tracing.
constraints.combination: Add compaction tokens when a request has compactions.

native_services.text: API tracing is supported. Set up the destination in the Claude Console with Admin permission.
SDK tracing works on any platform. API tracing lists only Claude Platform and Claude Platform on AWS.
SDK tracing works on any platform. API tracing lists only Claude Platform and Claude Platform on AWS.

components.exam_tie: D3.4. Expect a scenario where a bad outcome cannot be traced to its cause. The credited answer uses traces with one ID and cost per hop, not more text logs. (Inference)
components.trap: More prompt logs or longer retention keeps the blind spot. The logs hold no tool or retrieval hop.
components.decision_rule: Trace each hop that calls a model or a tool, and tie the hops to one trace ID.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario asks which tool call acted, pick the trace spans over the prompt text.

components.name: Usage, cost, and rate limit reports
components.first_principle: Usage and cost reports group token counts and dollars by workspace, key, and model, and response headers show live capacity.

nodes.label: Token usage by bucket and group

steps: Create an Admin API key for the organization.
Call the usage report endpoint with a bucket width of one hour or one day.
Add group_by for model, workspace, or API key to split the totals.
Call the cost report endpoint for daily totals in USD.
Read the anthropic-ratelimit headers on each response to track capacity left.
Compare the report totals with the Console Usage page before you reconcile. (Inference)
pros: Reports split spend by workspace, API key, model, and service tier.
Reports suit finance reconciliation with billing.
Response headers show live capacity without a separate call.
cons: Individual accounts cannot use the Admin API.
The cost report offers daily buckets only.
Claude Platform on AWS has no programmatic usage or cost endpoints.
use_when: Finance needs a monthly split of spend.
A team asks what one workspace spent in a week.
Capacity planning needs a trend of token use.
do_not_use_when: You need cost for one request in real time, so use the trace spans.
The platform is Claude Platform on AWS and you need a programmatic report.
A workspace key must call the report endpoints, which it cannot do.

constraints.choice: Use the cost report for daily totals in USD.
constraints.combination: Use the usage report with hourly buckets to find spikes.

constraints.choice: Read the anthropic-ratelimit headers on each response.
constraints.combination: Wait for the retry-after value before the next try on a 429.

constraints.choice: Use an Admin API key or a service account key that is not scoped to a workspace.
constraints.combination: Keep workspace keys out of report jobs.

constraints.choice: Read usage in the Console on Claude Platform on AWS.
constraints.combination: Programmatic endpoints are not available there.

native_services.text: Programmatic Usage and Cost endpoints are not available. Use the Console pages instead.
Admin API endpoints are not supported. Foundry does not return Anthropic rate limit headers.
The default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute. AWS enforces the requests per minute limits.

native_services.service: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed)
native_services.text: Google Cloud manages rate limits and quotas for this platform.

components.exam_tie: D3.4. Expect a scenario about spend attribution or throttling. The credited answer uses the usage and cost reports or response headers, not estimates from app logs. (Inference)
components.trap: Totals of input_tokens from each response look complete. That field counts only tokens after the last cache breakpoint.
components.decision_rule: Use the usage and cost reports for spend, and response headers for live capacity.
components.exam_tip: A spend-cap 429 has no retry-after header and stays failed until access resumes.

components.name: Claude Code and agent session telemetry
components.first_principle: Claude Code exports its own metrics and events to a destination you set, and managed settings keep that destination fixed.
steps: Set OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER and OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER to otlp.
Set the OTLP protocol and endpoint for your collector.
Leave OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS unset unless prompt text is allowed.
Set OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS to 1 to capture MCP call arguments.
Pin the OTLP endpoint and credentials in managed settings.
Check claude_code.session.count in the backend to confirm the pipeline.
pros: Standard metrics report cost and token use per session.
MCP activity events show the server, tool, and decision.
Managed settings keep the destination fixed for developers.
cons: Tool details can include call arguments, which may hold sensitive values.
Sign-in with a Claude account adds user.email to the attributes sent to your endpoint.
Subprocesses started by Claude Code do not inherit the OTel variables.
use_when: An organization needs cost and tool audit for developer use of Claude Code.
MCP call arguments must appear in the audit trail.
Managed settings can deliver the destination to every developer.
do_not_use_when: A repository setting must turn telemetry on, because Claude Code ignores OTel variables in project settings.
A developer needs prompt text in every session, since prompt text is off by default.
The Bash tool needs its own OTel variables, because Claude Code does not pass them down.

constraints.choice: Pin the endpoint and credentials in managed settings.
constraints.combination: Set the per-signal variables in managed settings when one signal needs its own collector.

constraints.choice: Send prompt content only to the endpoint you configure.
constraints.combination: Mask the prompt text attributes in your collector if policy forbids them. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use the console exporter for local checks.
constraints.combination: Set shorter export intervals only for short checks.

constraints.choice: Track claude_code.cost.usage in USD per session.

native_services.text: Telemetry carries only user.id and session.id. Attach user identity with OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES.

components.exam_tie: D3.4. Expect a scenario about audit of developer tool use. The credited answer uses managed telemetry settings and tool detail events. (Inference)
components.trap: A repository setting that enables telemetry looks simple. Claude Code ignores OTel variables in project settings, so the destination is not controlled.
components.decision_rule: Set telemetry destinations in managed settings, and keep prompt text off by default.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario asks for MCP call arguments, enable tool details and the logs exporter.
